newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MIDWEST WEEKEND RAINS SEEN UNDER ONE INCH - WSC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MIDWEST WEEKEND RAINS SEEN UNDER ONE INCH - WSC.

text.p: Two storm systems will bring chances for rain to the U.S. Midwest this weekend but Weather Services Corp meteorologist Joel Burgio said amounts would likely remain under one inch.
"There's two systems we're watching," Burgio said. "One is the showers and thunderstorms that will be covering the Delta today and tonight.
"It's expected to move further north on the weekend," he added. "We think that some of the shower activity will make it as far north as the southern part of Illinois, southern Indiana and Ohio."
The second storm was expected to bring showers to the western Corn Belt on Saturday and Sunday, moving east on Sunday and Monday.
"Between the two systems, we're going to stay with 0.25 to 0.75 inch with 40 to 60 percent coverage," Burgio said.
"The best chance (of high coverage) is southern Illinois and southern Indiana south of Indianapolis. Lower coverage would be in southeast Iowa into northwest and central portions of Illinois."

Next week should bring light showers in Missouri and the Ohio River Valley on Monday, Burgio said. Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday were expected to be fair with the next chance for rains coming the following weekend.
"There is no hot weather in the forecast any time between now and the middle of next week," Burgio said.
